chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Salih al-Nayli, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Allah (Exalted and Majestic) hates abundant eating. And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no escape for the son of Adam from a meal by which he sustains his body. So when one of you eats food, let him make a third of his belly for food, a third for drink, and a third for breathing. And do not fatten yourselves like the fattening of pigs for slaughter.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended proportion of the stomach for food, drink, and air according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) linking physical moderation to spiritual purity, warning that gluttony leads to the 'fattening' of the soul akin to pigs destined for slaughter. This hadith establishes the 'thirds' model of digestion as a prophetic tradition for maintaining health and facilitating worship, emphasizing that the stomach is not merely for sustenance but for spiritual readiness. The comparison to pigs highlights the contrast between those who eat solely for physical indulgence and those who eat to serve God.
